subject: Hosted API connection instability — customer-facing follow-up & postmortem
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@streamly.com>, support@streamly.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident notification: hosted API connection instability (Jun 14)

Hi Amelia / Streamly team,

I wanted to let you know we observed elevated connection churn against your realtime inference route between 08:20–09:05 PT this morning which temporarily increased error rate and caused some request retries. You may have seen elevated 5xx responses and slowed responses during that window. Our status page entry is live here: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-06-14-connection-oscillation

What happened (brief):
- Impact window: ~08:20–09:05 PT
- Symptom: short-lived connection instability and higher retry rates for the hosted generation endpoint (affects both streaming and non-streaming calls)
- User-facing: intermittent 5xxs and latency spikes; no data was deleted. We are investigating whether any request payloads were retried more than once and will call that out.

Immediate mitigation we applied:
- Shifted traffic to the standby routing pool to reduce retry amplification
- Increased prefetch backpressure thresholds to stabilize the fanout layer

Next steps:
- Internal postmortem and timeline; I will share a customer-facing postmortem draft within 24 hours
- We'll share required timestamps and a short remediation plan (kernel change + routing hardening)

I apologize for the disruption — we know low latency and reliability are critical for Streamly. If you can share any examples of failed requests or HubSpot IDs you saw impacted, that will help us correlate.

Attachments: incident-timeline-20270614.csv (timeline snapshot)

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@streamly.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:27:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident notification: hosted API connection instability (Jun 14)

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the heads up.

A couple quick asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether any inference requests were processed twice or delivered duplicate outputs to end users?
2) We need precise timestamps for errors and any request IDs you can share so our engineers can correlate with client-side logs.

We saw a spike in errors in our monitoring around 08:22–08:29 PT and then again around 08:48–08:51 PT.

Please loop in Marissa if you want to coordinate an engineer-to-engineer deep-dive.

—Amelia
Amelia Ruiz
Head of Platform, Streamly
amelia@streamly.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:18 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Incident notification: hosted API connection instability — prep for customer postmortem

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Amelia's note. Drafting the customer postmortem now. Quick internal notes we should agree on before I send: 

Root cause (prelim): oscillation in the prefetch/fanout layer under a short traffic burst plus a timing regression in our connection keeper that allowed more in-flight TCP/HTTP handoffs than expected. The combination magnified retry amplification.

Data integrity: no evidence of data exfiltration or deletes. There were a small number of duplicate-processing events caused by retries; we have identified ~34 request ids correlated to Streamly between 08:20:30–08:29:10 PT that were retried and processed twice. We should confirm exact dedup semantics with the logs.

Action items to propose to customer and track internally:
- Fix: release prefetch backpressure patch (runtime config + kernel guard) — estimated deploy in 72 hours
- Monitoring: add dedicated metric for prefetch-queue-oscillation and an alert at P95 of queue spikes — 48 hours
- Compensation: propose a one-week credit against Jun usage for the affected time window (discuss amount)
- Postmortem: customer-facing draft + internal timeline CSV attached (redwood-postmortem-draft.pdf to follow)

Can you both verify the count of duplicate requests and sign off on the proposed credit? I'll attach the draft and the timeline once I incorporate the exact request ids.

—Lauren

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@streamly.com>, support@streamly.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem and remediation plan — Jun 14 connection instability (Streamly)

Hi Amelia,

Thanks again for the patience while we completed the investigation. Attached is the customer-facing postmortem (redwood-postmortem-draft.pdf) and the incident timeline CSV we shared earlier. A short summary below: 

Incident summary:
- Window: 2027-06-14 08:20:18–09:04:55 PT
- Impact: intermittent 5xx responses and increased retries for Streamly-hosted inference requests; small number of duplicate-processing events (~34 request IDs identified and validated)
- Root cause: transient prefetch queue oscillation combined with a timing regression in our connection keeper. Under a brief traffic burst the fanout layer retried aggressively and triggered duplicate processing.

Remediation we are implementing:
1) Immediate fix: configuration change to prefetch backpressure thresholds (rolled out 2027-06-14 11:20 PT) — mitigated recurrence risk in short term
2) Medium-term fix: runtime kernel guard to enforce in-flight request limits in the fanout path (target deploy: 72 hours)
3) Monitoring: new metric and alert for prefetch-queue-oscillation and a daily regression job to validate keeper timings (target: 48 hours)

Customer impact and compensation:
- We recommend a one-week credit for the affected volume during the impact window. If that is acceptable we will generate a formal credit memo; please confirm preferred billing contact.

Attached: redwood-postmortem-draft.pdf (customer-facing), incident-timeline-20270614.csv
Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-06-14-connection-oscillation, https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/postmortems/streamly-20270614

If you'd like an engineer-to-engineer call to go through the timeline and logs, Marissa and Ben are available this week — let me know a preferred slot.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev-2 regression and prioritizing the kernel guard for the next rollout.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
